title: NY State Assembly · District 81
area: The Bronx: Riverdale, Kingsbridge, Van Cortlandt Village, Kingsbridge Heights, Marble Hill, Norwood, Woodlawn, and Wakefield

context.text: Incumbent Jeffrey Dinowitz (D) defeated Morgan Evers 64.6% to 35.2% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Evers, who had also won the Working Families Party primary, withdrew from that ballot line as well; Ballotpedia lists her as a withdrawn candidate and states she will not appear on the November ballot. As of this research, Dinowitz is the only candidate on the general-election ballot for this seat.

candidates.name: Jeffrey Dinowitz
candidates.currentRole: Member, NY State Assembly, District 81 (since February 1994)

summary.text: Jeffrey Dinowitz is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 81 in the Bronx, first elected in 1994. He chairs the Assembly's Codes Committee and previously chaired the Judiciary Committee, among others.

background.text: Dinowitz was born in 1954 and has lived in the Bronx all his life. He is a graduate of the Bronx High School of Science, Herbert H. Lehman College (CUNY), and Brooklyn Law School.
Before his election to the Assembly, he served as an Administrative Law Judge for the State of New York. He was elected a State Committeeman in 1978 and served as a District Leader from 1986 to 1994.

He chairs the Assembly Committee on Codes and serves on the Rules, Ways and Means, Health, and Election Law committees. He previously chaired the Judiciary, Corporations/Authorities and Commissions, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Aging, and Alcoholism and Drug Abuse committees.

He has authored numerous enacted laws, including the Anti-Human Trafficking Act (2007), the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (2014), the MTA Lockbox law (2018), the repeal of the non-medical vaccine exemption for schoolchildren (2019), and the COVID-19 Emergency Eviction and Foreclosure Prevention Act (2020/21).

priorities.text: "The affordability crisis is being felt across the Bronx and Jeff is determined to support working families and reduce costs. He's incredibly proud to have secured the Henry Hudson Bridge Rebate for Bronxites... Through his leadership, New York raised the minimum wage, easing the burden on thousands of working families."

"He is a proud co-sponsor of the New York for All Act, which would restrict the use of local resources and prohibit all law enforcement and state agencies from working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Patrol."

On housing: "He was the lead sponsor on the eviction and foreclosure moratorium during the pandemic... He has prevented landlords from removing rent protections in our neighborhoods, expanded access to resources for co-op owners, and brought in funding for affordable housing, including $10 million for the Amalgamated Houses."

On the environment: "He led the charge on passing the most aggressive climate action legislation in the nation – the Climate Change Superfund Act, which holds fossil fuel companies accountable for the damage they cause by requiring them to contribute $75 billion to the funding of critical infrastructure investments."

On healthcare: "He is a co-sponsor of the NY Health Act, which will create a single-payer healthcare system in New York and expand access to health insurance... He was a proud co-sponsor of the NY Reproductive Health Act that codified abortion access into state law."

record.text: Authored the Anti-Human Trafficking Act, enacted in 2007, establishing state penalties for human trafficking and support for victims.
Authored New York's adoption of the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, enacted in 2014.
Authored the MTA Lockbox law, enacted in 2018, to restrict diversion of dedicated transit funds.
Was the main sponsor of the 2019 law repealing the non-medical (religious) exemption from school vaccination requirements in New York.
Was lead sponsor of the COVID-19 Emergency Eviction and Foreclosure Prevention Act, enacted 2020/2021, to keep tenants and homeowners in their homes during the pandemic.
Chairs the Assembly Committee on Codes and serves on the Rules, Ways and Means, Health, and Election Law committees as of the 2025-2026 session.
Voted yes on S10113, which passed the Assembly 88–53, allowing a cannabis microbusiness licensee authorized for retail sales to also serve as a processor and cultivator for cannabis showcase events.
Voted yes on S3460, which passed the Assembly 92–49, granting employees access to their personnel records and requiring notice and a review opportunity for negative information in those records.

researchNotes: This race is uncontested on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot: Ballotpedia's candidate list and Morgan Evers' own profile both state that Evers, despite winning the Working Families Party primary, will not appear on the general-election ballot, leaving Dinowitz as the sole listed candidate. A prior internal slate snapshot (from July 2026) had listed Evers as still appearing on the WFP line; this file reflects the more recent Ballotpedia status as of September 25, 2026 and should be re-checked closer to the election in case her ballot status changes again.
